recognize_zh: CD30 染色中，右側大量大型細胞呈強的膜狀與核旁 Golgi 點狀陽性，左側則多為陰性小淋巴球；在 EBV 陽性黏膜皮膚潰瘍（EBVMCU）中，這群 CD30 陽性的何杰金樣大細胞是典型表現。
features: Numerous large cells with strong membranous and paranuclear Golgi-pattern CD30 staining
Positive cells concentrated in a dense zone (right) with scattered positive cells toward the left
Background small lymphocytes and endothelial/stromal cells negative
Positive cells vary in size, including large immunoblast- and Hodgkin-like forms
describe_en: CD30 immunohistochemistry shows strong membranous and Golgi-pattern staining in a significant subset of large atypical cells, which are densely aggregated in one area and scattered elsewhere, while background small lymphocytes are negative. The positive cells range from immunoblast-like to Hodgkin-like large forms. In the appropriate context of a sharply circumscribed mucosal or cutaneous ulcer in an immunosuppressed patient with EBER-positive cells, this pattern is consistent with EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer.

ddx.vs: cHL forms a mass or nodal disease rather than a circumscribed ulcer, and HRS cells typically lose B-cell markers, whereas EBVMCU large cells retain CD20/Oct-2 and are polymorphic.
EBV+ DLBCL forms destructive masses of sheets of large cells beyond a limited ulcer and does not regress with reduction of immunosuppression.
ALCL shows uniform strong CD30 in nearly all tumor cells with a T-cell or null phenotype and is EBV-negative.
These cutaneous CD30+ proliferations are T-cell derived (CD4+) and EBER-negative.
